preamble: Fortition of the alveolar lateral approximant /l/ to the voiced alveolar plosive /d/ keeps the alveolar contact but closes off the lateral airflow. In Malagasy, Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *l became d before *i (*lima 'five' > dímy). In Oti-Volta (Gur), Proto-Oti-Volta initial *l became d in Core Eastern Oti-Volta (Nateni, Mbelime, Ditammari, Byali) and, independently, in Nõotre, while the other Western Oti-Volta languages and Gurma keep l.

examples.note: Forms in Eddyshaw's transcription: j = [ɟ], y = [j], ɩ ʋ = [ɪ ʊ], a tilde below a vowel marks nasalization, ' marks a glottalized vowel; POV = Proto-Oti-Volta; the final syllable of nouns is a noun-class suffix. Kusaal lìi, Mooré lʋ̀ɩ, Nawdm luur- keep l.

examples.note: Nõotre is the only Western Oti-Volta language with d for POV initial *l; its sisters keep l (Kusaal lɔ̀kɔ̄, Mooré lòkó).
